stories.headline: Sources: Rams' Puka Nacua out 4-5 months after knee surgery, will miss playoffs
stories.summary: Puka Nacua's recovery time from MCL surgery is considered to be four to five months, sources told ESPN, meaning he will miss the playoffs.
stories.body:
Puka Nacua's recovery time from MCL surgery is considered to be four to five months, sources told ESPN, meaning the Los Angeles Rams star wide receiver will miss the rest of this season, including the playoffs.

Sources told ESPN that three doctors recommended that Nacua undergo the procedure, which is expected to have him healthy for the 2027 campaign.

Nacua's knee checked out clean aside from the MCL, according to a source. The operation was performed by team doctor Neal ElAttrache, a source told ESPN.

Rams coach Sean McVay said Friday that Nacua, who is serving a three-game suspension while on injured reserve, will likely miss at least the rest of the regular season after undergoing surgery Tuesday.

McVay added that the possibility of Nacua returning for the postseason was a scenario that the Rams "haven't thought about."

The NFL was unaware that Nacua had already undergone surgery when it imposed its suspension, a source told ESPN on Friday.

In seven games this season, Nacua had 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns. The two-time Pro Bowler suffered the knee injury, along with a turf toe injury, on the Rams' final offensive snap of their Week 9 victory over the Washington Commanders and was placed on IR on Nov. 12.

Nacua, 25, is playing on the final year of his rookie deal and is scheduled to be an unrestricted free agent this offseason.

stories.headline: Messi tracker: Goals, assists, key moments in 2026
stories.summary: ESPN provides game-by-game analysis of Lionel Messi's performances for Inter Miami and Argentina.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will aim for more success in 2026. His Inter Miami side captured its first MLS Cup title last season and will look to defend it -- and add further silverware too -- in its first season at Nu Stadium, the club's new home.

Messi also captained Argentina as they fell just one step short of defending their FIFA World Cup crown, losing 1-0 in extra time to Spain in the final of what could be his last tournament.

As the 39-year-old continues to feature for both club and country, ESPN will track his performances game-by-game, providing stats and analysis each time he pulls on a Herons or Albiceleste jersey.

Messi's 2026 tally:

Games played: 48
Goals: 41
Assists: 19

Nov. 21: Inter Miami 0-3 Columbus Crew
Ouch. That one hurt.

Miami and Messi are staring down the barrel of an early exit from the MLS playoffs after slumping to a 3-0 home loss to the Columbus Crew in Game 1 of their first-round series on Saturday.

The Argentine magician drew a blank as the Crew ran riot with a brace for Gonzalo Tapia either side of a goal from Taha Habroune.

Miami must now win when the best-of-three game series heads to Columbus for Game 2 on Friday to force a decisive Game 3 back in Miami on Dec. 2.

Nov. 7: Inter Miami 3-3 Charlotte FC
Although neither team had much at stake on Decision Day, Miami and Charlotte offered up an entertaining 3-3 draw at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

The Herons leapt out to a three-goal lead thanks to Ian Fray, Luis Suarez and Rodrigo De Paul -- with Messi, in a rare occurrence, not assisting any -- but were pegged back by the visitors to ensure both teams shared the points.

With the regular season now wrapped up, Miami's second-place finish in the East means Messi and Co. will face-off with the Columbus Crew in the first round of the postseason.

Nov. 1: New England Revolution 1-2 Inter Miami

Messi once again provided the magic touch for Miami, this time to ensure his team's spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Herons' marquee star set up a goal and scored the winner as Miami leapfrogged New England into second place in the Eastern Conference with one game remaining in the MLS regular season.

After going behind to a Dániel Gazdag goal, Miami responded with a strike from Germán Berterame -- set up by a deft backward header from Messi -- before the 39-year-old scored the winner in the 83rd minute. Sumptuous stuff.

Oct. 28: FC Cincinnati 2-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists for Messi in what was an eventful 2-2 draw with FC Cincinnati on Wednesday night.

Luis Suárez scored in the 61st minute to give Miami a 1-0 lead, and then the reigning MLS Cup champions needed some late-game heroics to salvage a point. They still fell to third in the Eastern Conference, after New England beat Red Bull New York 3-2 on Wednesday.

Oct. 24: Red Bull New York 2-0 Inter Miami
It has been an eventful few days for Messi. Just a day before the match, he traveled to Spain to receive the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, becoming the first individual soccer player to earn the honor.

He then returned to the United States and joined his teammates in New Jersey, starting on the bench before coming on in the 56th minute. However, he was unable to make an impact as the hosts secured a 2-0 victory, ending Miami's three-game winning streak.

Oct. 17: Atlanta United 1-3 Inter Miami
Messi scored twice in four minutes as Miami won 3-1 in Atlanta.

After Germán Berterame opened the scoring just before halftime, Messi doubled Miami's lead in the 56th minute, exchanging passes with Berterame before weaving past a defender and firing a low left-footed shot into the net.

Messi struck again in the 60th minute, latching on to a pass from Luis Suárez before beating his marker and slotting past goalkeeper Lucas Hoyos. The brace took Messi's MLS-leading tally to 25 goals for the season, while Miami extended its winning streak to three matches.

Oct. 14: Inter Miami 2-0 NYCFC
No goals, but after a scoreless first half, Messi helped break the deadlock by setting up Rodrigo De Paul for the opening goal. Germán Berterame later doubled Miami's advantage as the Herons secured their second consecutive win and clinched a spot in the MLS playoffs.

Oct. 10: Inter Miami 4-0 D.C. United

Back in the pink of Inter Miami, and back in the goals for Messi.

His two strikes sealed an emphatic 4-0 win for the Herons over D.C. United at Nu Stadium on Saturday night.

After Luis Suárez had Miami 2-0 up after 39 minutes Messi scored his first in the 47th, retrieving a pass from the Uruguayan before tapping in a shot inside the right post.

Messi then padded the hosts' lead in the 60th minute, latching on to Rodrigo De Paul's pass, before dribbling inside the area, eluding two United defenders and firing past goalkeeper Sean Johnson with a shot from 12 yards.

Oct. 6: Argentina 3-0 Benin

It was an emotionally charged night in Buenos Aires as Messi played his final international match for Argentina, the team that he had led to World Cup glory and two Copa América titles as captain.

The friendly match at the Estadio Monumental was goalless at halftime, but just a few minutes after the break Messi's in-swinging corner from the left was rattled home on the volley by Nicolás Otamendi.

Then, on the hour mark, Messi spotted Nico Paz in space 25 yards from goal. He fed a square pass with the outside of his boot to the Como player, who curled in a classy finish.

But the night undoubtedly belonged to Messi, and he fired a penalty into the top corner to cap off his 208th and final senior appearance for his country with his 126th goal.

Sep. 27: Columbus Crew 2-1 Inter Miami
Before heading to Argentina for his final international match, Messi gave Miami fans something to savor in Ohio.

From a set piece wide on the right wing and with most of those in the stadium, including those in the Columbus defense, surely expecting a cross, Messi's left foot sent the ball curling wickedly into the far top corner of the net.

Messi had chances to add to that tally in the second half but was denied from distance by Columbus goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and put another effort into the side netting.

Then Jamal Thiaré scored in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to give the Columbus Crew a stunning 2-1 win.

Sep. 20: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC

Messi's sublime curling free kick was not enough to inspire the Herons to a win against San Diego on Sunday night.

After falling behind to an Anders Dreyer goal in the 12th minute, 39-year-old Messi levelled the scores with beautiful set-piece shot in the 24th minute. His well-hit effort evaded a number of attackers and defenders before sneaking in at the far post.

Miami thought they'd won the match after Luiz Suarez fired the hosts ahead in the 74th minute, only for Dreyer to nab his second goal of the game and ensure the points were shared.

Sep. 16: Inter Miami 2-0 Cruz Azul

Another day, another trophy for Messi.

The Argentine master scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as the Herons defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.

Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez, before turning provider for Casemiro -- sending in a corner for the Brazilian to nod home.

Sep. 12: Inter Miami 2-2 Nashville SC
In a matchup between the two best teams in the Eastern Conference, the action went end to end, with Messi getting on the scoresheet for Miami's second goal off a Rodrigo De Paul assist as he continues to lead the Golden Boot race.

Ultimately, the teams settled for a point apiece, as the hosts failed to close the gap on Nashville at the top of the table.

Sep. 9: Chicago Fire 1-1 Inter Miami

Two or Europe's greatest club players took center stage in one of the United States' most iconic American football stadiums on Wednesday -- and a record crowd came out to watch.

Ex-Bayern Munich and Barcelona star Robert Lewandowski scored a trademark acrobatic goal in the 10th minute to give the Fire an early lead at the NFL home of the Chicago Bears.

But Inter Miami drew level shortly after halftime when Casemiro, another of the game's stars with a long history of playing in Europe before moving to MLS, headed home a Messi cross from a corner kick to make it 1-1.

The assist was Messi's league-leading 13th of the season. He also has league 18 goals and is the first player in MLS history with 30-plus goal contributions in three separate seasons.

Sep. 5: Inter Miami 2-2 Atlanta United
Messi was not as effective as he was in the previous matchup, but he did get an assist for Casemiro's opening goal. However, his team was unable to win as they had to settle for a point in a 2-2 draw.

August 29: Inter Miami 7-1 CF Montréal

Fans were treated to a Messi masterclass on Saturday as the Argentine magician registered four goals and an assist to help Miami to a club-record 7-1 victory over CF Montréal.

Messi scored with a deflected free kick in the 40th minute before netting after a stunning solo run in the 52nd. After supplying an assist to Luis Suárez, the 39-year-old then completed his hat trick and with a delicate chip over the goalkeeper with seven minutes of regulation time remaining.

He wasn't done yet.

Deep into stoppage time, Messi lined up a free kick and dispatched it with trademark precision into the top corner of the net. Legendary stuff.

August 22: Inter Miami 2-1 Toronto FC

Messi's 14th MLS goal of the season wasn't enough to prevent Inter Miami from slumping to their fourth loss in their last five games, losing 2-1 to Toronto FC at Nu Stadium on Saturday.

Messi found the net with a first-time finish from a Rodrigo De Paul through-ball with eight minutes remaining, but the home side's late rally fell short of salvaging a much-needed draw to bolster the Herons' pursuit of first-placed Nashville SC in the Eastern Conference.

August 19: Inter Miami 2-2 Philadelphia Union

Messi is back scoring goals, but unfortunately, his Miami side is not back to winning ways. The Argentine scored Miami's second goal of the night as both teams finished with 10 men. Miami are now winless in their last four matches.

August 15: Nashville SC 4-1 Inter Miami
It was not the best night for Messi in Tennessee. The Argentine missed yet another penalty -- his third straight for club and country -- and they suffered a heavy 4-1 loss to their Eastern Conference rivals. However, he did get an assist for Telasco Segovia's equalizer at halftime before Miami lost control in the second half.

August 12: Inter Miami 2-3 Club León
Just days after the passing of his father, Messi came off the bench in the second half to try to help Miami continue in the Leagues Cup after they were leading 1-0. However, it ended in a 3-2 loss which saw them eliminated in the league phase after a second straight loss, coming off defeat to Monterrey last weekend with Messi away at the memorial for his father.

August 5: Inter Miami 4-2 Atlético de San Luis

Lionel Messi made his first start for Inter Miami since returning from the World Cup and picked up right where he left off, scoring a stellar pair of goals to guide his team to a come-from-behind 4-2 rout of Atlético de San Luis in its first game of the 2026 Leagues Cup.

Messi's first goal was an exquisite volley, redirecting Noah Allen's cross from the left flank while running at full speed. Miami's third goal of the opening half -- and Messi's second on the night -- came on the back of some intricate buildup play with Allen once again setting up his team captain, this time in the center of the area where he tiptoed through two defenders and buried a close-range strike past Andrés Sánchez.

The goal made Messi the all-time leading scorer in Leagues Cup history with 14, one ahead of LAFC's Denis Bouanga since the expanded competition began in 2023.

August 1: Inter Miami 2-2 Columbus Crew
Messi made his return to action for Inter Miami on Saturday, 13 days after tasting defeat with Argentina in the World Cup final. The Miami talisman started on the substitutes' bench before being introduced in the 53rd minute of the Herons' 2-2 draw with the Columbus Crew at Nu Stadium in Miami.

July 19: Spain 1-0 AET Argentina

Sunday proved to be a bridge too far for both Messi and Argentina, falling in extra time to Spain in the World Cup final.

With La Roja controlling the match basically from start to finish -- Argentina didn't register a shot on target during regulation time -- Messi had few opportunities to impact the game. Indeed, the 39-year-old was given a 3/10 in ESPN's post-match player ratings.

Still, as Mark Ogden points out, the 2026 tournament was a memorable one for Messi and cemented his status as the GOAT, if it were ever in doubt.

July 15: England 1-2 Argentina
Messi made another statement in his 205th appearance for Argentina, this time in his first-ever match against England in a World Cup semifinal. With so much at stake for both nations, Messi once again proved decisive despite not getting on the scoresheet.

He first provided the assist for Enzo Fernández's superb strike to level the match in the second half before delivering a pinpoint cross for Lautaro Martínez's headed winner, sending the reigning champions into yet another World Cup final after another dramatic encounter.

Messi has now recorded either a goal or an assist in all seven of Argentina's matches at this World Cup, and he will have the opportunity to lift the trophy for a second time when Argentina face Spain in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

July 11: Argentina 3-1 Switzerland
It was a relatively quiet night by Messi's standards as his goalscoring streak came to an end, but his influence on the match stayed the same. He set up Alexis Mac Allister's opening goal for Argentina against Switzerland, and although the match went to extra time, the defending champions won 3-1 thanks to two late goals in the second half of extra time.

Messi's quest to retain the World Cup now continues into the semifinals, where Argentina will face England for the first time in over 20 years. The clash in Atlanta -- one of international soccer's most storied rivalries -- will decide a spot in the final.

July 7: Argentina 3-2 Egypt
It was another dramatic outing for Messi and Argentina, who rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Egypt 3-2 in Atlanta and book their place in the World Cup quarterfinals. As is so often the case, Messi was at the center of the action. Minutes after Egypt opened the scoring, he missed another penalty, but he quickly made amends by setting up Cristian Romero for Argentina's first goal. Messi then scored the equalizer -- his eighth goal of the tournament -- before Enzo Fernández completed the comeback with the winner. Argentina will now face Switzerland in Kansas City for a place in the semifinals.

July 3: Argentina 3-2 Cape Verde
Messi suffered a major scare in Miami Gardens on Friday evening in the round of 32, but it ultimately ended well for Argentina. He opened the scoring with his seventh goal of the tournament, extending his World Cup tally to 20 goals while finding the net in a record eighth consecutive World Cup match. Cape Verde twice fought back -- once in the second half and again in extra time -- but the world champions eventually prevailed 3-2 after extra time to book a meeting in the round of 16 with Egypt.

June 27: Jordan 1-3 Argentina
Messi didn't play the full 90 minutes in Argentina's 3-1 win over an already-eliminated Jordan, but he still made his mark during a 30-minute cameo in Texas. The 39-year-old scored a free kick for his sixth goal of the tournament and his 19th career World Cup goal, becoming the first player ever to score in seven consecutive World Cup matches. Even at 39, he's still got it.

June 22: Argentina 2-0 Austria
Another chapter in an already unparalleled career. Lionel Messi scored twice in Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria to help his team qualify for the round of 32 and become the outright leading goalscorer in men's and women's FIFA World Cup history with 18 goals. After missing an early penalty, he responded by breaking Miroslav Klose's 12-year-old record and then added a second late on to break Marta's record. All just two days before turning 39.

June 16: Argentina 3-0 Algeria
In his 200th appearance for Argentina and sixth World Cup, Lionel Messi sent a message to the world just days before his 39th birthday: he still has it. His first-ever World Cup hat trick powered Argentina to victory in their group-stage opener, while his 16th tournament goal saw him draw level with Miroslav Klose for the most goals in World Cup history.

June 9: Argentina 3-0 Iceland

Messi, working his way back from muscle fatigue ahead of the start of the World Cup, came on in the 70th minute of a pre-tournament friendly in Auburn, Alabama and scored from the penalty spot right afterward.

It was Messi's 911th career goal for club and country and 117th goal for Argentina and made him the oldest scorer in the country's soccer history.

May 24: Inter Miami 6-4 Philadelphia Union

Messi registered two assists in a scintillating performance against Philadelphia on Sunday but, unfortunately, no one was focused on results come the end of the game.

That's because, in the very last game before the World Cup, Messi left the field in the 73rd minute and headed straight to the locker room after grabbing his left thigh.

Now, supporters around the world are holding their collective breath while they wait and see if the injury has scuppered the 38-year-old's chance of appearing at a sixth World Cup.

May 13: FC Cincinnati 3-5 Inter Miami

Two goals and one assist marked yet another spectacular contribution from Miami superstar Messi on Wednesday. The Argentine magician was instrumental as the Herons fought back from 3-2 down to eventually beat Cincinnati 5-3 at TQL Stadium in Ohio.

May 9: Toronto FC 2-4 Inter Miami

It was a day of star power. Not only were Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez and Sergio Reguilón all on the score sheet for the Herons, so was Messi -- and he added a pair of assists, too.

While Miami has yet to taste victory at its new home, it continues to take care of business on the road. Saturday's win in Toronto extended the club's unbeaten record away from home in 2026 to seven games, picking up six wins and one draw in the first few months of the season.

May 2: Inter Miami 3-4 Orlando City

Messi notched a goal and an assist on Saturday in what ended up being an astonishing collapse for Inter Miami at Nu Stadium.

The Herons were leading 3-0 after Messi's classy 33rd-minute strike, but gifted the visitors four goals -- including a Martín Ojeda hat trick -- to once again miss out on a victory at their new home ground. Orlando's comeback from three goals down marks only the third time in MLS history that a team has claimed all three points after trailing by three or more goals.

As for Messi's Miami, only twice has an MLS team had a longer winless run -- now up to four for the Herons -- to open up a new stadium.

April 25: Inter Miami 1-1 New England Revolution
Messi again failed to get on the scoresheet as Miami put in a fatigued second-half performance that saw them come from a goal down against New England. It was another draw -- and another game without a win at their new home, Nu Stadium.

April 22: Real Salt Lake 0-2 Inter Miami
No goals or assists from Messi as Miami visited America First Field on Wednesday, but the fans did get treated to sumptuous strikes nonetheless.

Rodrigo De Paul's opener in the 80th-minute was stunning curler from outside the box and then, almost immediately after the restart, Luis Suarez made it 2-0 with a well-struck volley.

The victory moves Inter Miami into outright second in the MLS Eastern Conference.

April 18: Colorado Rapids 2-3 Inter Miami

Another moment of Messi magic bagged all three points for Inter Miami on Saturday.

With scores level in the 79th minute, the Argentine icon danced his way past a number of Colorado defenders before curling home an outrageous effort into the far corner.

The strike -- Messi's second of the match after converting a penalty in the first half -- helped Miami to their first win under interim coach Guillermo Hoyos.

Hoyos, who had been serving as club's sporting director, took over coaching duties after Javier Mascherano unexpectedly left the club due to personal reasons last week.

April 11: Inter Miami 2-2 Red Bull New York
Miami and Messi are still waiting for a first win at Nu Stadium after a 2-2 draw with Red Bull New York on Saturday night.

Messi didn't register a goal or assist, but did help set up Germán Berterame's second-half strike that gave Inter Miami its first lead at its new home ground, but 17-year-old Adri Mehmeti's first career goal in the 77th minute secured a point for the visitors.

April 4: Inter Miami 2-2 Austin FC
Inter Miami opened Nu Stadium the only way it knows how: With a Messi goal. The No. 10 began the move in trademark style with a left-footed pass to a teammate before moving past a defender and arriving in the box at just the right time to head past goalkeeper Brad Stuver.

March 31: Argentina 5-0 Zambia
It was the last day of the month and perhaps the last game for Messi playing for Argentina playing in his native country, but they put on a show defeating the African side Zambia 5-0. Messi scored the second goal for Lionel Scaloni's side as focus will shift now to Miami until the beginning of the World Cup.

March 27: Argentina 2-1 Mauritania
In his first game for his country in 2026, Messi only played the second half as Argentina won 2-1 against Mauritania at the mythical La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, as the World Cup champions continue to prepare to defend their title this summer in North America.

March 22: NYCFC 2-3 Inter Miami

It was a thrilling encounter in the Bronx, as the Argentine star helped his team to a 3-2 win over NYCFC, which also included another trademark free kick goal, now beginning his course for potentially 1,000 career goals. Only 99 goals left!

March 18: Inter Miami 1-1 Nashville SC

Messi may have made history on Wednesday night, becoming just the second men's player in history to score 900 career goals, but it wasn't enough to seal Miami's progress in the Concacaf Champions Cup.

The Argentina legend found the back of the net in the seventh minute at Chase Stadium, but his strike was cancelled out by Nashville's Cristian Espinoza -- sealing the Herons' tournament exit on the away goals rule.

March 11: Nashville SC 0-0 Inter Miami
A drab night for Messi and Co. in the Concacaf Champions Cup. Plenty of possession but few shots on target mean that the Herons will return to Chase Stadium know a win will be needed to ensure progression.

March 7: D.C. United 1-2 Inter Miami

It was quite an eventful week for Messi. Just days before Miami's match against D.C. United, Messi and the entire squad visited the White House and met President Donald Trump and were eager to put on a show for the sold-out crowd of over 70,000 at Baltimore's M&T Bank Stadium.

And they did just that, with a 2-1 win over D.C. United. Messi, of course, scored Miami's second and is now one goal away from 900 career goals.

March 1: Orlando City 2-4 Inter Miami

Well, that blip didn't last long! Messi and Miami roared back into life with a 4-2 thrashing of Orlando on Sunday thanks to the 38-year-old's wizardry.

Things looked ominous for the Herons after the first 45 minutes, down 2-0 and looking on course to start the MLS season with two bleak losses.

But two goals and an assist from Messi in the second half dragged the visitors back in the game and helped secure Miami their first points of the season.

Feb. 21: LAFC 3-0 Inter Miami
Messi and Miami aimed to start 2026 firing on all cylinders, but it was the hosts who spoiled the defending MLS Cup champions' opener at the LA Coliseum. In front of a sellout crowd of 75,673 -- the second-highest attendance in MLS history -- Miami were outplayed, with LAFC's Denis Bouanga getting a goal and an assist in a convincing home victory.

The main talking point, however, emerged after the final whistle. Messi was initially reported to have gained unauthorized access to the officials' locker room after video circulated showing him near the area. However, it was later reported that no league policy had been violated and Messi was cleared of any wrongdoing. Miami will now turn its attention next weekend against fellow Florida side Orlando City.

stories.headline: 76ers survive in clutch again despite Herro's 50: 'Got to finish better'
stories.summary: The 76ers survived 50 points from Tyler Herro, nearly blowing a 10-point lead late, before once again coming out on top in the clutch.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- In a season full of wins that keep this fanbase stressed until the final buzzer, the Philadelphia 76ers' 132-129 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday followed suit.

The Sixers survived a career-high 50 points from Bucks guard Tyler Herro, who nailed a contested fadeaway 3-pointer at the end of regulation that would have tied the score, but an official review determined Herro released the ball just after time expired.

After the game, Sixers center Joel Embiid, who led the team with 26 points, 17 rebounds and nine assists, praised Herro as "a top five player in the league."

The win moved the Sixers to 14-3, which is tied for the NBA's best record and their best 17-game start since 2000-01, when they last reached the NBA Finals. And yet, much of the conversation after their most recent victory centered on how they're winning games.

"Obviously, we wanted to close the game out a lot better," said LeBron James, who finished with 21 points, six rebounds and six assists. "But a team like that, we know they're scrappy. They're going to play as hard as they can for their minutes. It's about just getting the win, but we can learn from a lot of things that we didn't do well tonight."

The Sixers have been in a lot of close games this season. They are a league-leading 12-0 in clutch-time games, a stat that reflects both how good they've been at finishing games and their struggles to build and maintain leads against lesser teams like the Bucks, who have just one win this season.

"We've got to play a 48-minute game," said guard Tyrese Maxey, who had 17 points. "We're playing like 40-minute games or 24-minute games, 30-minute games. And soon, we're going to have to put together a 48-minute game."

​Milwaukee -- as most teams have this season -- pounced on the Sixers early, jumping out to a seven-point first-quarter lead. The Sixers quickly overcame that deficit and were in control for much of the second half. They led by 10 points with just over two minutes left, but the Bucks stormed back and nearly sent it to overtime.

"I try not to complain too much about any win in this league ... we got to finish a little better," 76ers coach Nick Nurse said.

Despite the Sixers' struggles to put away teams this season, James said he has been impressed with how well they are already playing, particularly with their willingness to pass.

"I think early on, like preseason, it looked a little weird. Guys were like overpassing, you know, looking weird," he said with a smile. "But that's been great. And I think for the majority, our defense has been really good for the majority of the season. Tonight wasn't so great, but we've been really good defensively throughout the course of the season."

Still, James said there is room for improvement, which he welcomes: "We don't want to be great in November. That would be weird."

The Sixers next host the Portland Trail Blazers on Monday.

stories.headline: Mets, A.J. Ewing reach 8-year, $95M extension, sources say
stories.summary: The Mets and 22-year-old center fielder A.J. Ewing have agreed to an eight-year, $95 million contract extension, sources confirmed to ESPN.
stories.body:
The New York Mets and center fielder A.J. Ewing are in agreement on an eight-year, $95 million contract extension that includes a club option for a ninth season, sources confirmed to ESPN's Jeff Passan on Saturday.

The deal buys out Ewing's two remaining pre-arbitration years, his three arbitration years and at least three free agent years. It is pending a physical.

Ewing's deal is the largest contract extension for a pre-arbitration player in franchise history. David Wright -- arguably the greatest position player in Mets history -- previously held the mark with a six-year, $55 million deal he signed in August 2006.

Ewing, 22, was selected by the Mets in the fourth round of the 2023 draft out of high school. The Ohio native made his major league debut in May and was one of the few bright spots in another disappointing season in Queens.

While concluding his rookie season as a below-average hitter -- he posted a 97 wRC+ -- he showed flashes as a future leadoff hitter and supplied plus baserunning and elite defense at a premium position.

After a hot start to his career, Ewing recovered from a deep midseason slump to slash .318/.390/.489 over his last 25 games. He finished with a .252 batting average, 11 home runs, 25 steals and a .700 OPS in 120 games. The total package produced a 2.0 fWAR.

The Mets' outfield appears to be set for years to come with Ewing in center, fellow rookie Carson Benge in right and franchise cornerstone Juan Soto in left. Benge, another elite defender, was also part of the Mets' silver lining in 2026, finishing second in National League Rookie of the Year voting after batting .282 with 20 home runs, 22 steals and a .776 OPS in 156 games.

SNY first reported news of the deal.

stories.headline: AFL Draft 2026: Grading the draft hauls for every club
stories.summary: The 2026 AFL Draft has been run, but which team won? ESPN's draft expert Jasper Chellappah has handed down five As and two Ds after this year's two-night affair.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL Draft has been run and done, so let's get into grading each team's haul. Night one was headlined by a Brisbane points matching debacle, with the Swans landing Caylen Murray.

It flipped the script for teams down the order with the Saints and Pies landing their preferred prospects thanks to Brisbane's three-point miss on Murray.

On night two there was a clear directive from clubs to draft based on list need. With the crop of talent 15 past 40 so even this year, clubs were focused on specific roles that suit the modern game and it resulted in bolting mature-agers earning main list opportunities.

These draft grades aren't just based on the calibre of talent brought into the club - it was a lot easier for Port Adelaide and Carlton to land star youngsters than North Melbourne and Geelong. It takes into account live trading, value on each pick and positional fits at the club.

These are ESPN's draft grades for every club after the 2026 AFL Draft.

READ: 'No one saw it coming' - Inside the Swans' draft heist that landed a Lions Academy star

Adelaide
Pre-draft hand: 15, 32, 35, 43, 54

Selections: Toby Krasna (14), Xavier Ladbrook (34), Sam Tassone (44)
There was a clear plan from the Crows to address their transition ball movement, and they've done so here. Krasna is an outside midfielder that really came on this year with his class in space. He runs hard both ways, plays with flair on the ball and is incisive with his foot skills in the forward half.

Xavier Ladbrook will take time to develop as a 202cm key defender that needs time in the gym, but his running base and length gives him an exciting platform. It was rounded out with local dasher Sam Tassone who has some raw, developable traits with speed out of defence.

The Crows passed up Anthony Long after Geelong's bid on the NGA forward.

Grade: B-

Brisbane
Pre-draft hand: 21, 27, 28, 45

Selections: Kodah Edwards (27), Archie Van Dyk (28), Jackson Phillips (29), Archie Spencer (36)

We haven't seen a bid matching debacle quite like Brisbane's on night one when they fell three points short of keeping Caylen Murray. The Lions cornered themselves and found no trade partner on the clock.

It meant they unexpectedly carried three selections back to back early on night two, opting for two South Adelaide products in Edwards and Van Dyke as they addressed their midfield mix.

Edwards captained SA and has versatility to play on-ball or through the forward 50, while Van Dyk has the size and skill to develop rapidly in a professional environment.

Phillips looks a natural wingman at the next level with good ball use off both feet and disciplined running patterns. He looks most likely to play senior football early next year, and they rounded out with dashing defender Archie Spencer.

Grade: D

Carlton
Pre-draft hand: 13, 18, 31, 50, 59, 67, 73

Selections: Cody Walker (3), Harvey Spawton-Guy (32), Jackson Watkins (37), Ethan Herbert (46)

A nice mix of prospects for the Blues began with the arrival of Cody Walker early on night one. The gifted midfielder has Brownlow upside in his prime as a natural ball-winner that puts speed on the game with aggressive movement.

WA's Harvey Spawton-Guy will be looked at as a tall to develop at both ends of the ground - he competes superbly in the air and that attack on the footy bodes well. Jackson Watkins plays with power in the forward half as a smaller type and Ethan Herbert's upside as a ruck of the future is enticing with his ball-winning and skill around the ground a point of difference.

Grade: A-

Collingwood
Pre-draft hand: 11, 30, 63, 64, 65

Selections: Sam Gayfer (12), Gus Kennedy (31), Jordan Knapp (41), Koby LeCras (62)

This is some sort of result for the Pies. They had Gayfer circled on their board from a long way out and were delighted to find him available. His courage and strength in the air at a combine-record vertical leap will be a nightmare to defend.

Kennedy is one of the great characters of the class and plays with a lot of energy off halfback, while Knapp is an exceptional ball magnet through the midfield but will need to build size at the next level.

Rounding out a significant haul was one of the big sliders Koby LeCras. The nephew of premiership Eagle Mark, the 192cm forward can roam up wings with a big engine and is a beautiful kick around goals off his preferred left.

Grade: A

Essendon
Pre-draft hand: 1, 17, 25, 69, 75, 78, 80 (plus second round compensation pick)

Selections: Ethan Drever (2), Archie Elliott (17), Harvie Cooke (21), Jack Pickett (26), Blake Justice (55)

The Bombers had a lot of work to do on each night and they will come away happy with the draft haul. Drever is the perfect complement to previous drafts through the midfield as the outside speed and damage, rating him as the No. 1 player in the open pool.

They paired him with best mate Archie Elliott which produced the best moment of night one as he was pulled out of the crowd at Marvel Stadium. The small forward is an excellent aerialist and has a defensive edge to his game that appeals.

Harvie Cooke was the Talent League's best and fairest and will suit a high half forward role at the next level, while the 194cm Jack Pickett is the big upside swing in the second round as the most accurate set shot to come through the pathways in some time. He will take time as he rehabs a torn ACL and MCL.

The Dons rounded it out with NGA Blake Justice who will be a slow starter to pre-season with a hamstring, but the 192cm midfielder has a unique blend of speed, agility and height that is exciting to develop.

Grade: B+

Fremantle
Pre-draft hand: 19, 40, 58, 61, 68

Selections: George Dimer (18), Kane Johnston (42), Jake Medved (57)

The Dockers have some ready-made options to add depth on a flag tilt. They were delighted that Dimer got through a host of suitors late on night one, and he looms as an immediate Switkowski replacement. Dimer is ultra-clean below his knees at 173cm and sets up teammates selflessly.

Kane Johnston is a 24-year-old tall out of the WAFL that's played his best footy in the forward 50 but could be utilised in defence. His body is ready to compete and the athleticism is AFL level.

Fremantle pinched Jake Medved out of the Swans Academy to round out their night. The utility has played in just about every position this season but could be best used as a wingman with his ranginess and endurance base.

Grade: C+

Geelong
Pre-draft hand: 36, 55, 60

Selections: Lachie Hicks (38), Anthony Long (56), Zach Stevens (60)

This was a quintessential Cats draft. They entered late on night two and immediately took a swing on one of the best athletes in the draft. Hicks has the speed-endurance blend Geelong covets, covering big distances and racking up the ball all season for the Western Jets.

Anthony Long was one of five(!) academy prospects they bid on late. The Crows NGA prospect is Izak Rankine's cousin and brings sharp agility and forward 50 creativity at 184cm.

Finally, Zach Stevens was the classic local product pick out of South Barwon. He's possibly the fastest product to be drafted and as a half forward showed flashes in the VFL and at Talent League levels.

Grade: B

Gold Coast
Pre-draft hand: 8, 70, 72, 77

Selections: Leo Steed (10), Elliott Himmelberg (63), Jamarra Ugle-Hagan (64)

The Suns took one live pick to the draft via Ben King's compensation. They opted for the midfield option in WA's Leo Steed, whose clean hands, strong transition running and fantastic work ethic rocketed his stocks this year. Steed has balance and selflessness to his game.

They rounded out the draft with two rookie elevations.

Grade: C

GWS
Pre-draft hand: 9, 20, 26, 57

Selections: Ethan Matthews (6), Jake Eime (13), Andrio Sousa (45)

Matthews is the best academy prospect GWS has had since Tom Green, and the earliest they've ever taken in a draft. The Giants moved up as far as they could so their residual draft pick would sit in the teens and with that pick they opted for Jake Eime.

A very Giants-esque selection, the SA product is an aggressive rebounder off halfback with the dare to tuck the ball and take on opponents. He can finish off transition in the forward half with good disposal and forms an exciting combination with Lachie Ash.

On night two Andrio Sousa presented as a fantastic athlete to develop on a wing or forward flank, though in isolation trading pick 20 to the Power for a future second-rounder was a poor return.

Grade: B-

Hawthorn
Pre-draft hand: 29, 37, 66, 74

Selections: Benji Van Rooyen (30), Cooper Hodge (58), Keenan Boi (59)

The Hawks targeted a real list need with Van Rooyen, the younger brother of Melbourne's Jacob. He's a legitimate ruck size and uses his physicality in the air well, enjoying the best championships of any ruck this year playing for WA.

The Cats made sneaky bids on Luke's son Cooper Hodge and Keenan Boi, with the latter sliding through to make for a comfortable bid match. Hodge's best traits come in the contest where he's tough and aggressive, while Boi has a lot of power in the forward half.

Grade: C+

Melbourne
Pre-draft hand: 4, 14, 48, 51, 79

Selections: Mitch Harris (7), Lochie Burrows (15), Ben Forster (49), Kaie Sullivan (52)

The Dees had another two first-rounders to play with and opted for the top key defender in Harris. His form a SANFL League level to finish the season cemented his top-10 status and Melbourne will look to him and Disco Turner as the future combination in defence.

Lochie Burrows is one of the best characters in the draft and gives the Dees huge flexibility as a halfback or hard-nosed on-baller. Ben Forster is a role player swing late in the draft with the wingman running hard both ways and offering neat skills in space. Kaie Sullivan was the late-season boater out of the Stingrays after a huge finals campaign elevated his stock off half forward.

Grade: B

North Melbourne
Pre-draft hand: 33, 49, 62

Selections: George Gale (23), Seb Marsic (35), Aidan McCartney (54)

The Roos traded their future first-rounder to get in for George Gale, such was their plaudits of the hardened youngster. He runs hard as an outside midfielder and has the size to eventually transition inside, but looks like a disciplined role player that will allow others to shine early in his career.

Seb Marsic was a bolter on night two as a big, physical key forward. He kicked seven goals in a game that North's Ollie Griffin kicked four at the other end.

The Aidan McCartney bid was matched late on night two with the 195cm son of Jason finding his way to Arden St.

Grade: B-

Port Adelaide
Pre-draft hand: 7, 12, 22, 24, 34, 46

Selections: Dougie Cochrane (1), Clancy Snell (19), Wil Malady (20), Wil Antrobus (25), Gabriel Patterson (39), Angus White (47)

The draft of the year goes to Port Adelaide. Dougie Cochrane was only the start for them, but it was a big one with the consensus best prospect in the pool becoming Port's first-ever No. 1 pick.

Shrewd live trading landed picks 19 and 20 and they grabbed sliders. Clancy Snell is one of the best interceptors in the crop and at 197cm will play on a range of forwards. Wil Malady is an upside swing on the clear talent. The 190cm forward is athletic and brilliant in the air.

Wil Antrobus was an early call at pick 25 but fits a clear need out of defence. His left leg is lethal in open play and he can be relied upon to kick in. They finished off with local products - Gabe Patterson plays with power in the forward half while Angus White has rehabbed an ACL this year but adds speed through the midfield.

Grade: A+

Richmond
Pre-draft hand: 2, 5, 44, 76 (plus second round compensation pick)

Selections: Arki Butler (4), Harry Van Hattum (8), Noah Williams (22), Harry Franz (51)

Richmond landed open prospects at 1 and 3 in ESPN's Power Rankings. Arki Butler, the match-winning medium forward, and Harry Van Hattum, the standout ruckman, are upside swings into the future. Neither can be expected to hit the ground running fully next year but could spearhead the Tigers into a new era.

Noah Williams was a smart choice at 22 with his competitiveness through the midfield and in defence giving him the versatility to play early. Richmond finished their draft with Harry Franz, a high-flying 194cm defender out of SA that plays with physicality.

Grade: A+

St Kilda
Pre-draft hand: 10, 16, 41

Selections: Gustavo Teixeira (11), Tyson Bradley (16), Lewis Houndsome (43)

The Saints could not believe their luck when Brisbane didn't match on Caylen Murray and Gus Teixeira slid all the way through to 11. A genuine first overall pick chance at stages this year, Teixeira has power, class and upside in the forward half.

They nabbed another bayside product at 16 in Vic Metro MVP Tyson Bradley. At 195cm he should grow into the physical key defender that takes on the big forwards at AFL level.

St Kilda finished off night two with Lewis Houndsome, a big key forward that's played well through the ruck but struggled with injuries after a promising bottom-age campaign.

Grade: A

Sydney
Pre-draft hand: 6, 38, 39, 47

Selections: Caylen Murray (9), Brady Wright (40), Mitch Knevitt (48), Mason McGroder (61)

It was a bold and brilliant coup to land Murray, but it remains to be seen if he was best available for the Swans at that point. It's a clear list need with the departure of Nick Blakey in the off-season; Murray offers dash and class off halfback, being one of the most reliable distributors in the crop and offering midfield upside.

Brady Wright was prolific for Werribee in the VFL, and the 194cm goalkicker is a best 23 candidate next year after winning the Fothergill-Round-Mitchell Medal. They added to their mature-age pickups with delisted Cat Mitch Knevitt, whose size around the ball could prove valuable.

Mason McGroder didn't attract a bid until pick 61 which made matching a formality. The long jumper won silver at the U20s World Games in Oregon this year and presents as one of the best athletes to ever come into the AFL system.

Grade: B+

West Coast
Pre-draft hand: 3, 23, 56 (plus second round compensation pick)

Selections: Heath Mellody (5), Jake Soutar (24), Harper Banfield (65)

The pickups are solid for the Eagles, but the way they approached this draft is up for debate for a second straight year. Despite being armed with more list spots than any team in the competition thanks to assistance packages, they were once again caught out this week, not turning over enough primary list spots.

West Coast traded a valuable second-rounder into next year, receiving North's future first in the heavily-compromised 2027 draft -- Tasmania's first. As a result they only took the three picks this time around -- a disappointment for a rebuilding side -- all from WA.

Heath Mellody is the best WA prospect since Luke Jackson, providing the outside run and carry that clubs covet. He's an elite kick and fits alongside Harley Reid and Willem Duursma superbly. Jake Soutar is the readymade option and they went early on the 20-year-old. He's a natural interceptor at 190cm and will likely play on third talls next year.

They rounded out the night by taking father-son Harper Banfield with their natural selection after a bid didn't materialise. He's a strong-bodied midfielder with an elite endurance base.

Grade: D+

Western Bulldogs
Pre-draft hand: 42, 52, 53, 71

Selections: Khaled El Souki (33), Jack Riding (50), Sam Devers (53)

It was an uncomfortable wait through night one and early parts of night two for a bid on El Souki to arrive. The small forward NGA landed in an ideal part of the draft for the Dogs to match and the eruption from El Souki's family and friends was worth the wait. His physicality, left foot and goal sense gives him an elite platform to blossom at the Dogs.

The 26-year-old Jack Riding has toiled away with Werribee to earn this opportunity, and is drafted with a role for him in the forward 50. He's a beautiful crumber of the ball and has mixed it in senior football already.

Sam Devers is an upside play as a 189cm defender that straight lines the ball and puts speed on the game. He took time returning this year after a shoulder reconstruction.

Grade: B

stories.headline: Tom Brady tops list of athletes who became owners
stories.summary: The legendary quarterback is a member of an exclusive list of athletes that includes LeBron James, Serena Williams and Wayne Gretzky.
stories.body:
Tom Brady is getting (back) into the ownership game.

On Friday, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network that the former superstar quarterback had bought shares in the English soccer giants Chelsea. Brady's purchasing of Chelsea shares comes after he departed the ownership group of another English club, EFL Championship side Birmingham City, earlier in the month after originally becoming a minority owner with a 3.3% stake.

Brady's latest interest isn't his only foray into the world of ownership -- he also owns a 5% minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, purchased in 2024, and he also has a stake in the Las Vegas Aces.

The NFL legend is far from the first athlete, active or former, to enter the ownership sphere. Here are other athletes who are now team owners:

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Atlético Madrid

In October 26 news broke that the star Oklahoma City Thunder guard would be joining the club as an investor.

"I am excited to officially join the group of shareholders of Atlético de Madrid," Gilgeous-Alexander said in the club's post. "This is a club with a long history at the top of European football, and I am grateful for the opportunity to be part of its future."

Jason Kidd -- Everton

In April 2025, English Premier League club Everton announced that then-Dallas Mavericks coach Jason Kidd would be adding a different title to his résumé: ownership group member. The news came after Kidd joined Roundhouse Capital Holdings, which is part of the Friedkin Group -- the U.S. firm that completed its takeover of Everton's ownership the previous December.

Vince Carter, Tracy McGrady, Jozy Altidore -- Buffalo Bills

In December 2024, the Bills announced Carter, McGrady and Altidore were among 10 limited partners the team was adding to its ownership group. Both McGrady (New York Knicks) and Altidore (New York Red Bulls) played for New York-area teams, while Carter spent time with the Brooklyn Nets (who were known as the New Jersey Nets at the time) and was McGrady's teammate on the Toronto Raptors (who are closer to Buffalo than NYC-based teams).

Tom Brady -- Las Vegas Aces, Las Vegas Raiders, Chelsea

The Las Vegas Aces, the reigning WNBA champions, have added to their championship credentials. Seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady acquired a minority stake in the team whose majority owner is Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis.

"I have always been a huge fan of women's sports, and I admire the work that the Aces' players, staff, and the WNBA continue to do to grow the sport and empower future generations of athletes," Brady said in a statement. "To be able to contribute in any way to that mission as a member of the Aces organization is an incredible honor."

Brady attended an Aces game in May 2022 and sent gifts to star Kelsey Plum. Plum and other Aces players were excited to have Brady as part of the team.

He also added the Las Vegas Raiders to his resume after his purchase of minority stake in the franchise was approved by NFL teams owners on Tuesday. The deal was agreed on in May 2023, but it took owners 17 months to give their approval over concerns he was receiving too much of a discount from majority owner Mark Davis.

Brady was also a minority owner of Birmingham City, a club in English soccer's second-tier Championship, but sold his shares in November 2026. He purchased shares in Chelsea later that month.

Lewis Hamilton -- Denver Broncos

The Broncos' ownership group added racing royalty in August 2022. Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton has a stake with the Walton-Penner group, which purchased the team in June 2022.

Hamilton, 37, has the Formula One record for most race wins and has won the Formula One title seven times. The ownership group, which purchased the team for $4.65 billion, is led by Walmart heir Rob Walton and includes former U.S. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, who also has a stake.

In April, Hamilton joined with Serena Williams in a consortium led by former Liverpool chairman Martin Broughton in an attempt to buy Premier League club Chelsea.

"He is a champion competitor who knows what it takes to lead a winning team," Walton said in a statement.

Marshawn Lynch -- Seattle Kraken

Lynch spent 13 seasons in Seattle with the Seahawks, but his new sports venture in the state of Washington is on the ice. On April 18, he joined the Seattle Kraken ownership team as a minority investor. The former NFL running back will be a part of the NHL's "Hockey is for Everyone" campaign and Kraken owner Tod Leiweke said Lynch expressed interest in shadowing him to learn hockey CEO operations.

"This is something I never would have imagined," Lynch said to CNBC in a statement. "I always dreamed of playing on a professional team but owning one is something special. As I look back on some of my accomplishments...I'm [going to] continue to count my blessings."

Grammy Award-winning artist and Seattle native Macklemore also joined the Kraken ownership team with Lynch.

Wayne Gretzky, Steve Nash and Dustin Johnson -- Las Vegas Desert Dogs

Wayne Gretzky is a big lacrosse guy? Yep, you read that right. The Great One may have made his name on the ice, but before Gretzky was the pride of the Edmonton Oilers he was a bona fide lax bro.

"The national sport of Canada is box lacrosse," Gretzky said. "I started playing lacrosse on a team at the age of six and played all the way until I was 16 years old. I have a great love for the game in the sense I really think that box lacrosse was such a crucial part of the success I ultimately had in ice hockey."

Because of this, it shouldn't be completely surprising that the hockey legend is linking up with 2020 Masters champion Dustin Johnson, NBA Hall of Famer and current Brooklyn Nets head coach Steve Nash and Nets owner Joe Tsai as part of a star-studded ownership group for the National Lacrosse League's newest expansion team in Las Vegas, the Desert Dogs.

Dwyane Wade -- Utah Jazz

Seeing Dwyane Wade support any team other than the Miami Heat is decidedly jarring. In April, the three-time NBA champion purchased an ownership stake in the Utah Jazz, joining majority owner and team governor Ryan Smith, and expressed a desire to take an active role in the franchise. D. Wade made good on his promise. He could be seen courtside throughout the season; he took action when an unsettling fan incident went down during the postseason, and he became a mentor to then-Jazz star Donovan Mitchell.

The former Miami Heat star also added to his portfolio with something a bit closer to home. Wade, a Chicago native, joined the ownership group of the WNBA's Chicago Sky.

"It's a great opportunity to be a part of the league in its very early stages. ... Growth is going to happen, and so I want to be a part of the growth of this league," Wade said.

Kevin Durant -- Philadelphia Union, NJ/NY Gotham FC

In June 2020, Brooklyn Nets star Kevin Durant purchased a 5% stake in MLS' Philadelphia Union, and he has an option to purchase an additional 5% at a later date. Durant also had engaged in talks about purchasing part of D.C. United the year prior, but he said the discussion never progressed.

Durant expanded his portfolio in May of this year, after being named as a minority owner of the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) club NJ/NY Gotham FC.

Thirty Five Ventures (35V), a company co-founded by the two-time NBA champion and entrepreneur Rich Kleiman, made a significant investment to acquire a stake in the club, marking the company's second investment in a professional soccer team.

Renee Montgomery -- Atlanta Dream

Former Atlanta Dream guard Renee Montgomery made history in February as part of a three-member investor group that was approved to purchase the team. Montgomery is the first former player to become both an owner and executive of a WNBA franchise. The ownership change followed pressure on former Republican Sen. Kelly Loeffler to sell her share of the Dream, after she angered WNBA players with her opposition to the league's racial justice initiatives.

Patrick Mahomes -- Kansas City Royals

Patrick Mahomes is no stranger to winning. While the Kansas City Royals can't exactly say the same, you can't rule out that the quarterback's winning ways might rub off on the franchise now that he is part of their ownership group. If Mahomes' status as an icon in Kansas City was in question (it wasn't), this move surely cemented it. Becoming a baseball owner made sense on several levels for the Chiefs' QB1. Not only was Mahomes -- who played baseball in college -- a legitimate pro prospect, his father, Pat Mahomes, spent 11 seasons in Major League Baseball. He also had to find some way to put that $503 million contract extension to good use.

Venus and Serena Williams -- Miami Dolphins, Angel City FC

Winning major titles and making history, that's what the Williams sisters do. In 2009, Venus and Serena became the first Black female minority owners in the NFL by purchasing a part of the Miami Dolphins. Musicians Jimmy Buffett, Gloria and Emilio Estefan, Fergie and Marc Anthony also bought shares in the team -- the Dolphins' ownership group is nothing if not eclectic. Then, last year, Serena Williams became part of the star-studded Angel City FC ownership group bringing a NWSL team to Los Angeles in 2022.

Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy -- Angel City FC

When Angel City FC arrived on the scene it did so in style. Before we even knew the Los Angeles based NWSL club's name, we knew it had superstar backing like no other. Among the 14 former USWNT players who are part of the group are Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy. I would have named Lauren Holiday, Shannon Boxx, Rachel Buehler, Amanda Cromwell, Joy Fawcett, Tisha Venturini Hoch, Angela Hucles, Shannon MacMillan, Saskia Webber and sisters Lorrie Fair Allen and Ronnie Fair Sullins, but I was really trying to stay true to my whole "I'm only going to name 20 athletes" thing from the intro. There are also a bunch of celebrities in the mix, but we don't have that kind of time.

Michael Jordan -- Charlotte Hornets

While we're on the subject of owners who haven't had the type of success we grew accustomed to in their playing days, I would be remiss if I didn't mention the GOAT. In 2010, Michael Jordan became the first ex-player to be a majority owner in the league when the NBA's Board of Governors unanimously approved his $275 million bid to buy the then Charlotte Bobcats in his home state of North Carolina. After a decade of underwhelming years, things look to be on the up for the now Hornets with Rookie of the Year LaMelo Ball providing a long-awaited spark in the organization. Never forget when his dad said he could beat MJ one-on-one ... good times.

Alex Rodriguez -- Minnesota Timberwolves, Minnesota Lynx

I don't know what part of this purchase feels less ideal to me, that Alex Rodriguez and his 50-50 business partner Marc Lore are only pursuing acquiring the Minnesota Timberwolves and Lynx after their original plan to buy the New York Mets failed or that Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards had no idea who former MLB star A-Rod was. Either way, the $1.5 billion deal is expected to close around July 1.

David Beckham -- Inter Miami

David Beckham, iconic soccer player and remains-to-be-seen owner. Beckham -- who is incredibly hands on with the franchise -- is part of an ownership group which was initially called Miami Beckham United but now operates under the name Miami Freedom Park LLC. Beckham and Inter Miami have seemingly been riddled with controversy since the club's inception in 2018. But all those problems could be a thing of the past if Lionel Messi decides to head to MLS. Hey, stranger things have happened.

LeBron James -- Liverpool

Back in 2011, LeBron James and manager Maverick Carter became minority owners of Premier League club Liverpool after Fenway Sports Group, which purchased the team in 2010, became the sole marketer of James' global rights. The deal has turned out to be pretty lucrative for James -- his original stake in the club, valued at about $6.5 million, had grown to about $32 million as of 2018. In 2019, Liverpool won the Premier League for their first top-flight league title in thirty years.

James Harden -- Houston Dynamo, Houston Dash

James Harden might not be in Houston anymore, but the former Rockets superstar's presence is still felt in the city. The Beard purchased a 5% stake in the group that controls MLS' Houston Dynamo and NWSL's Houston Dash in 2019. Boxer Oscar De La Hoya is also part of the group. The Dash won their first NWSL title last year, so he's probably feeling pretty good about that investment.

Russell Wilson and Ken Griffey Jr. -- Seattle Sounders

What do Russell Wilson, Ken Griffey Jr. and Macklemore have in common? They are all part of the Seattle Sounders' ownership group. Wilson, along with his wife, musician Ciara, purchased a stake in the team in 2019 -- just in time for them to win an MLS Cup title. Griffey Jr. and his family followed suit in November 2020.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic -- Hammaraby

Seemingly everything Zlatan does makes people react intensely, and that remained true when he purchased part of Swedish team Hammaraby back in 2019. Fans of Malmo, another Swedish team where Zlatan started his professional career, reacted by vandalizing a statue of Zlatan outside the team's home stadium, placing a toilet seat around one of its arms.

Magic Johnson -- Los Angeles Dodgers

Big LA guy. In 2012, Lakers great Magic Johnson was part of a group that bought the Los Angeles Dodgers from Frank McCourt for a record $2 billion. At the time, the price shattered the mark for a sports franchise. Magic kept it real at the time of purchase when explaining his role in recruiting free agents, saying that while he can't talk hitting or pitching with players, he "can talk winning." If recent history is any indication (in case you blacked out all of 2020 -- the Dodgers won the World Series), it worked.

stories.headline: Champions League upstarts Como suffer Moise Kean injury blow
stories.summary: Como forward Moise Kean is set to be out injured for at least two months and could miss Champions League games against Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.
stories.body:
Como forward Moise Kean is set to be out injured for at least two months, his coach Cesc Fabregas said on Friday, and could miss Champions League games against Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.

The 26-year-old Italy forward injured his right leg against Belgium in the Nations League this week but the latest issue was with his left leg, Fabregas said.

- Meet Como's Nico Paz, the heir to Lionel Messi's No. 10 shirt for Argentina

- UCL talking points: First upsetting United, now NINE goals!? Are Como the real deal?

Como previously said Kean needed treatment on an injury in practice after returning from national team duty.

In its first season in the Champions League, Como have adapted stunningly fast with a 9-1 win at Lens and a pair of 4-1 victories at home to Manchester United and RB Leipzig.

Como are fourth in the 36-team standings ahead of hosting AEK Athens on Tuesday. The league phase for Como finishes with Real Betis next month and titleholders PSG, one of Kean's former clubs, and Barcelona in back-to-back weeks in January.

Kean arrived at Como on an initial season-long loan from Fiorentina and his injury leaves just Tasos Douvikas as a proven striker until the January transfer window. Kean has been limited to just four appearances for Como so far this season.

Como are fifth in Serie A and host Cagliari on Saturday.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Kangaroos bounce Kiwis for fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup title
stories.summary: The Kangaroos have won a fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup, toppling New Zealand 32-12 in Brisbane.
stories.body:
The Kangaroos have punished a disappointing New Zealand, with Reece Walsh running riot in a 32-12 World Cup final waltz.

There was an expectation the Kiwis, searching for their second Cup title and first since 2008, would push Australia all the way after a two-point loss in a pulsating tournament opener.

But the visitors struggled from the outset in Brisbane on Sunday night, Jamayne Isaako's kick-off floating long in a sign of things to come.

Walsh dazzled at fullback for the Kangaroos, his pace, vision and wicked footwork too much as he helped lay on two tries and generally wreak havoc around the ruck and close to the line.

Conversely, Walsh's New Zealand opposite Kalyn Ponga -- International Rugby League's Golden Boot winner on Thursday night -- was unable to get into game.

Australian hooker Harry Grant and halves Tom Dearden and Cam Munster completely outplayed their error-riddled opposites, while the Kangaroos' pack muscled up.

Dearden laid on two first-half tries for Liam Martin with well-timed short balls, while Bradman Best was rewarded for an inspired chase-down tackle of Jahrome Hughes with a try soon after.

When Tom Trbojevic scored to begin the second half it was 28-6 and effectively game over.

Jack Bostock completed his breakout season with a try in each half for Australia.

It was the Kangaroos' fourth consecutive title and 10th in the last 11 tournaments, dating back to 1975.

stories.headline: Cardinals rule out rookie Carson Beck, turn to 40-year-old Josh Johnson vs. Chiefs
stories.summary: Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck has been downgraded to out, paving the way for 40-year-old Josh Johnson to start against the Chiefs.
stories.body:
Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, paving the way for 40-year-old Josh Johnson to get his first start for Arizona.

Coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that Arizona was preparing Johnson to start after Beck experienced back spasms again this week. Beck didn't practice Thursday or Friday after being a limited participant Wednesday.

Sunday against the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium will be Johnson's first start since Week 18 of last season and just his 12th career start after being a fifth-round pick in 2008. He is 2-9 overall.

Although he doesn't have a lot of starting experience compared with his longevity in the league -- Arizona is his 15th NFL team -- the situation Johnson is in feels "familiar."

"It's kind of my testimony my whole life, just the unknown, what can happen," Johnson said. "And so just always just being in the moment, being prepared for myself. I've been in this situation, particularly in the NFL, a lot. So more excited than nerves, I would say."

Johnson said he is in a constant state of staying ready, which has been a factor in him playing into his 40s. At this point in his career, he's used to it.

Last season, Johnson replaced injured Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota in Week 16 and then started the final two games of the season after not starting since 2021.

"My job is to always be ready no matter what, no matter how the situation," Johnson said. "So I focus more on that than what's not ideal. And so this is just the next step of that process, and it keeps happening and so you just keep accepting it. You don't fight it, you embrace it, and you just go with it."

Johnson said his experience working with LaFleur in 2020 when LaFleur was the San Francisco 49ers' receivers coach and in 2021 with the New York Jets when LaFleur was the offensive coordinator will help "tremendously" on Sunday.

"Just understanding how he calls the game first and foremost is very important because you don't have to get antsy, like, 'Oh, what is he going to do in these moments?'" Johnson said. "And Mike is pretty consistent. He's been consistent. I've always been a big fan of him as a playcaller, as a coach, just in general."

Johnson is also familiar with Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo, having played against him and being on the Giants when Spagnuolo was New York's defensive coordinator in 2016.

Despite a familiarity and comfort with LaFleur, Johnson is also realistic about how Sunday can go after spending less than two weeks learning the offense.

"I also understand that everything ain't going to be perfect," Johnson said. "I'm not trying to go out there and be perfect. I'm trying to go out there and play winning football."

stories.headline: Messi, Miami staring at early playoff exit after Columbus rout in Game 1
stories.summary: Inter Miami and star Lionel Messi are facing the prospect of an early exit from the MLS playoffs after a 3-0 home loss to the Columbus Crew.
stories.body:
Defending champion Inter Miami and star Lionel Messi are facing the prospect of an early exit from the MLS playoffs after a 3-0 home loss to the Columbus Crew in Game 1 of their first-round series Saturday.

Gonzalo Tapia scored twice for Columbus, on either side of a goal from Taha Habroune, to stun a star-studded Miami team that played most of the game with 10 men after a 36th-minute red card for defender Gonzalo Luján.

Miami must now win when the best-of-three game series heads to Columbus, Ohio, for Game 2 on Friday to force a decisive Game 3 back in Miami on Dec. 2.

The second-seeded Miami, boasting Golden Boot winner and prohibitive MVP favorite Messi, finished 13 points clear of seventh-seeded Columbus in the regular season.

The Crew were in last place in the Eastern Conference on Sept. 1 but entered the MLS postseason having won its past six regular-season matches -- the longest active streak in the league.

It was another disappointing performance for Inter Miami in its first season playing at Nu Stadium -- the 26,700-seat venue that opened this year. Miami won just six of 17 regular season matches at its new home since playing its first game there in April, and was shut out for the first time at the venue on Saturday.

From early on, Miami played a major role in its own downfall.

Goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair committed an unforced error by bringing down Tapia in the box after rushing off his goal line to concede a penalty just eight minutes in. The Columbus forward made no mistake from the spot to put Miami in an early hole.

Miami had chances to pull level, with Messi being spectacularly denied by Columbus' United States international goalkeeper Patrick Schulte and Luis Suárez poking a shot just wide of the post with the goal at his mercy.

At the other end, though, Miami was grateful for St. Clair partially redeeming himself with some smart saves of his own.

But the home side's hopes of a comeback were dented further when Luján was sent off in the 36th minute after being shown two yellow cards.

Messi, too, was showing signs of frustration and was given a yellow card after taking a throw-in straight into the face of Tapia from just a couple of feet away.

The scoreline being just 1-0 at the interval was perhaps the only silver lining for Miami from the first half.

But it didn't stay that way for long. Exploiting glaring deficiencies in the Miami defense, Columbus scored twice in six early second-half minutes.

First, Habroune feasted on a through ball from Brais Méndez to side-foot home past St. Clair before Tapia grabbed his second after easily turning Yannick Bright and running clear to score.

Columbus' dominance was such that interim coach Laurent Courtois could afford to take off Tapia with more than 30 minutes to go in an effort to preserve his legs and ensure he didn't receive a second yellow card that would rule him out of Game 2.

Courtois has overseen a dramatic turnaround for the Crew just to make it this far after languishing in last place in the Eastern Conference on Sept. 1.

Miami, in contrast, limped into the playoffs and must now produce an immediate resurgence of its own after a loss that means it has now won just five of its past 18 MLS matches.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Chelsea in 'fragile moment' as Caicedo injury adds to pain of Leeds rout
stories.summary: Another crisis might be unfolding at Chelsea, just a few months into Xabi Alonso's tenure.
stories.body:
Home defeats to big rivals. Injuries to key players. One of the worst defenses in the Premier League.

Another crisis might be unfolding at Chelsea, just a few months into Xabi Alonso's tenure.

- Raya exits with injury as Arsenal held by Newcastle: 'Never good news'

- Man City at a crossroads as a shell of themselves

- VAR review: Should Haaland's goal vs Fulham have been disallowed

"We're in a fragile moment," Alonso said Saturday after seeing his team overrun in a 4-1 home loss to Leeds, who hadn't won at Stamford Bridge this century.

"We need to be tougher," he added. "It's something mandatory in this competition.

Already without major players in striker João Pedro and defender Maxence Lacroix because of injuries, Chelsea fell apart against Leeds following the enforced withdrawal of Moisés Caicedo in the 22nd minute after the Ecuador midfielder landed awkwardly on his back while making a challenge.

Despite going ahead within three minutes through Emmanuel Emegha on his first start, Leeds equalized almost immediately through Noah Okafor and dominated the second half, scoring through Dominic Calvert-Lewin -- via the penalty spot -- Okafor again and then U.S. midfielder Brenden Aaronson.

Leeds -- whose rivalry with Chelsea dates back to the 1960s and early '70s -- last beat the London club away in 1999. Less than a month ago, Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 2018. Before the international break, Chelsea lost 1-0 at Sunderland, which started that match in last place.

Chelsea, one of the biggest spenders in Europe in recent seasons, has tumbled toward midtable and are putting in lethargic performances even though the team doesn't have the hindrance of European competition this season.

"After we lost Moises, we lost completely the momentum," Alonso said. "Until then we were doing OK, but from that moment they started believing and we started not believing. After that, we never got the good feeling and were not able to come from the pressure. It completely changed.

"I'm not feeling [let down]. We do it as a team, as [a] collective. We need to support each other. We need to find solutions to do better because this will happen. There were moments that we were not competing at the level required. But the physicality, the duels, it's not the only explanation. The mentality part we can do better."

Chelsea has now conceded 20 goals in 11 games, with only last-place Crystal Palace and promoted teams Ipswich and Coventry letting in more.

Information from The Associated Press and PA contributed to this report.
